previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted the day after discharge following an allogeneic stem cell transplant for CML in myeloblastic crisis, presenting with severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and worsening abdominal pain. She had not taken her immunosuppressive medications, including tacrolimus, due to confusion at home. Imaging revealed pancolitis and later new ascites. Colonoscopy showed no infection or graft-versus-host disease. Tacrolimus levels were initially high, and dose reduction led to improvement in symptoms and resolution of ascites. She gradually resumed oral intake, remained stable, and was discharged with a revised immunosuppressive regimen including mycophenolate and prednisone. Thrombocytopenia persisted but was stable, likely related to medication effects.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis

radiology_notes.text:
CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST

COMPARISON:  ___.

HISTORY:  Graft versus host disease on skin biopsy with new cough and
low-grade fever.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axially acquired images of the chest were obtained.  No IV
contrast was administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were performed.

FINDINGS:

CT CHEST:  Scattered axillary lymph nodes are identified, none of which meet
CT criteria for pathologic enlargement.  A prominent pretracheal lymph node
(2, 15) is unchanged.  Calcified left hilar nodes are unchanged (2, 30). 
There is no pathologically enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.  The
airways are patent to the subsegmental level.  There is no evidence of pleural
effusion. There is minimal pericardial thickening versus effusion, unchanged. 
A calcified granuloma within the right upper lobe (2, 21) is unchanged.  There
is no focal consolidation or pneumothorax.  There has been interval resolution
of patchy ___ opacities in the right upper lobe. Coarse calcification
in right breast tissue, unchanged.

BONE WINDOWS:  There is no suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesion identified. 
Degenerative changes of the thoracic spine are noted.

IMPRESSION:  No focal consolidation or effusion. Interval resolution of prior
opacity in right upper lobe.

MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with AML status post SCT with GVHD with
worsening abdominal pain.  Please do CT p.o. and IV contrast to evaluate for
signs of inflammation/infection.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images from the abdomen and pelvis were obtained after
administration of IV and oral contrast.  Multiplanar reformatted images
(axial, coronal, sagittal) were generated.

Comparison with prior CT of ___.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN:  Partially visualized lungs with bilateral basal atelectasis.
Partially visualized heart and pericardium appear unremarkable.

The liver enhances homogeneously, without evidence of intra- or extra-hepatic
biliary dilatation.  Hepatic and portal veins are patent without evidence of
thrombosis.  Gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, stomach, small
bowel appear unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance promptly and symmetrically
without evidence of hydronephrosis.  Again noticed is a small simple cyst in
the lateral upper pole of the right kidney, overall unchanged.  There is no
intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free air or free fluid.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The bladder, distal ureters, pelvic loops of large and
small bowel are within normal limits.  Genitourinary structures are
unremarkable.  There is no free fluid or free air.  There is no
lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no osseous lesion suspicious for malignancy.

Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were reviewed, confirming axial
findings.

IMPRESSION:  Normal abdominal and pelvic CT.
